'''''Halodule wrightii''''' is an [[aquatic plant]] in the [[Cymodoceaceae]] family.<ref name=KewPOWO>{{cite web|url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:602957-1|title= Halodule wrightii Asch.|author=<!--Not stated-->|date=n.d.|website=Plants of the World Online|publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|access-date= September 26, 2020}}</ref> It is referred to by the common names '''shoal grass''' or '''shoalweed''', and is a plant species native to seacoasts of some of the warmer oceans of the world.

''H. wrightii'' is an herb growing in [[salt-water]] [[marshes]] in [[intertidal]] regions, often [[Underwater|submerged]] at [[high tide]] but [[Emergent plant|emergent]] at [[low tide]].<ref name=Godfrey1979>Godfrey, R. K. & J. W. Wooten. 1979. Aquatic and Wetland Plants of Southeastern United States Monocotyledons 1–712. The University of Georgia Press, Athens.</ref>

==Taxonomy==
This plant was named after [[Charles Wright (botanist)|Charles Wright]], who was an American botanist and collector. In 1853 and 1856 Wright participated in a surveying expedition and discovered ''Halodule wrightii''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Indian River Lagoon Species Inventory|url=https://www.sms.si.edu/irlspec/Halodu_beaudet.htm|website=Smithsonian Marine Station at Fort Pierce}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Berlin.|first=Gesellschaft Naturforschender Freunde zu|date=1868-01-01|title=Sitzungsberichte der Gesellschaft Naturforschender Freunde zu Berlin.|journal=Sitzungsberichte der Gesellschaft Naturforschender Freunde zu Berlin|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/7914997#page/27/mode/1up|language=en|volume=1868|issn=0433-8731}}</ref><ref>Ascherson, Paul Friedrich August. 1897. Die Natürlichen Pflanzenfamilien 2: 37.</ref>

Some publications cite [[United States|US]] specimens by the synonym, ''Halodule beaudettei'',<ref>Hartog, Cornelis den. 1964. Blumea 12: 303.</ref><ref>Hartog, Cornelis den. 1960. Pacific Naturalist 1(15): 4–5, f. 2a–c.</ref> but the two names represent the [[Synonym (taxonomy)|same species]].<ref name=fna>{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=222000075|title=''Halodule wrightii'' in Flora of North America @ efloras.org|website=www.efloras.org|access-date=2017-02-03}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Phillips |first1=Ronald C. |title=On Species of the Seagrass, ''Halodule'', in Florida |journal=Bulletin of Marine Science |date=1 July 1967 |volume=17 |issue=3 |pages=672–676 |url=https://www.ingentaconnect.com/content/umrsmas/bullmar/1967/00000017/00000003/art00009 }}</ref><ref>McMmillan, C. 1991. Isozyme patterning in marine spermatophytes. In: L. Triest, ed. 1988+. Isozymes In Water Plants. Opera Botanica Belgica 1+ vols. Belgium, Meise. Vol. 4,: pp. 193--200.</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tropicos.org/ImageFullView.aspx?imageid=34787|title=Image|website=www.tropicos.org|access-date=2017-02-03}}</ref>

==Description==
Seagrass is a marine [[Flowering plant|angiosperm]] that possesses conductive tissue, shoot systems, [[rhizome]]s and flowers.<ref name=Gallegos1994>{{cite journal |last1=Gallegos |first1=Me |last2=Merino |first2=M |last3=Rodriguez |first3=A |last4=Marba |first4=N |last5=Duarte |first5=Cm |title=Growth patterns and demography of pioneer Caribbean seagrasses ''Halodule wrightii'' and ''Syringodium filiforme'' |journal=Marine Ecology Progress Series |date=1994 |volume=109 |pages=99–104 |doi=10.3354/meps109099 |bibcode=1994MEPS..109...99G |doi-access=free }}</ref> It has flat leaves up to {{Convert|20|cm|abbr=on}} long, dark reddish-brown, with a few teeth on the margins. The fruits are spherical to egg-shaped, about 2 mm across.<ref name=fna/><ref name=Godfrey1979/><ref>Novelo, A. & L. Ramos. 2005. Vegetación acuática. Cap. 5: 111–144. In J. Bueno, F Álvarez & S. Santiago, Biodiversidad del Estado de Tabasco. CONABIO-UNAM, México.</ref>

==Distribution==
This plant is mainly found in muddy coastal marsh waters and off the coast of many Caribbean islands.<ref name=Gallegos1994/> It has been reported from [[Texas]],<ref>Correll, D. S. & M. C. Johnston. 1970. Manual of the Vascular Plants of Texas i–xv, 1–1881. The University of Texas at Dallas, Richardson</ref> [[Florida]], [[Louisiana]], [[Mississippi]], [[Alabama]], [[North Carolina]], [[Maryland]],<ref name=fna/><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Halodule%20wrightii.png BONAP (Biota of North America Project) floristic synthesis,  ''Halodule wrightii''] Image</ref> [[Yucatán (state)|Yucatán]], [[Quintana Roo]], [[Tabasco]],<ref>Cowan, C. P. 1983. Flora de Tabasco. Listados Florísticos de México 1: 1–123.</ref><ref>Sousa Sánchez, M. & E. F. Cabrera Cano. 1983. Flora de Quintana Roo. Listados Florísticos de México 2: 1–100.</ref><ref>Novelo R., A. & A. L. H. 1994. 239. Cymodoceaeceae. 6: 15–16. In G. Davidse, M. Sousa Sánchez & A.O. Chater (eds.) Flora Mesoamericana. Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México, México, D. F.</ref> [[Costa Rica]],<ref>Hammel, B. E. 2003. Cymodoceaceae. In: Manual de Plantas de Costa Rica, B.E. Hammel, M.H. Grayum, C. Herrera & N. Zamora (eds.). Monographs in systematic botany from the Missouri Botanical Garden 92: 456–457.</ref> [[Belize]],<ref>Balick, M. J., M. H. Nee & D.E. Atha. 2000. Checklist of the vascular plants of Belize. Memoirs of The New York Botanical Garden 85: i–ix, 1–246.</ref> [[Panama]], [[Cuba]], [[Trinidad and Tobago]], [[Venezuela]], [[Brazil]] and [[Cape Verde]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Creed |first1=Joel C. |last2=Engelen |first2=Aschwin H. |last3=D´Oliveira |first3=Emanuel C. |last4=Bandeira |first4=Salomão |last5=Serrão |first5=Ester A. |title=First record of seagrass in Cape Verde, eastern Atlantic |journal=Marine Biodiversity Records |date=December 2016 |volume=9 |issue=1 |page=57 |doi=10.1186/s41200-016-0067-9 |s2cid=7494405 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

In [[California]], it was intentionally introduced into the [[Salton Sea]] from Texas almost a century ago, but died out a long time ago.<ref>Hickman, J. C. 1993. [https://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_cpn.pl?27572&expand=1 The Jepson Manual: Higher Plants of California] 1–1400. University of California Press, Berkeley.</ref>

==Ecology==
These aquatic plants form sea beds and increase habitat stabilization through constant shoot and rhizome production. The string-like structure of the seagrass decrease water [[turbidity]] and movement of substrate whether it is sand or mud.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hall |first1=Lauren M. |last2=Hanisak |first2=M. Dennis |last3=Virnstein |first3=Robert W. |title=Fragments of the seagrasses ''Halodule wrightii'' and ''Halophila johnsonii'' as potential recruits in Indian River Lagoon, Florida |journal=Marine Ecology Progress Series |date=3 April 2006 |volume=310 |pages=109–117 |doi=10.3354/meps310109 |jstor=24870011 |bibcode=2006MEPS..310..109H |doi-access=free }}</ref> Seagrass beds function as an incubator for young juvenile fishes. They provide shelter from predators and reduce competition with other species. ''Halodule wrightii'' also supplies food resources to several species of fish, invertebrate marine life and [[manatee]]s.<ref name="Pereira et al 2010">{{cite journal |last1=Pereira |first1=Pedro H.C. |last2=Ferreira |first2=Beatrice P. |last3=Rezende |first3=Sérgio M. |title=Community structure of the ichthyofauna associated with seagrass beds (''Halodule wrightii'') in Formoso River estuary - Pernambuco, Brazil |journal=Anais da Academia Brasileira de Ciências |date=September 2010 |volume=82 |issue=3 |pages=617–628 |doi=10.1590/S0001-37652010000300009 |pmid=21562690 |doi-access=free }}</ref> This species of plant has the ability to adapt to various levels of [[salinity]] and temperatures.

''H. wrightii'' is able to reproduce sexually and asexually, however, flowering in this species is rare.

==Conservation==
Recreational activities, like jet skiing and boating, damage and uproot seagrass beds with ease in shallow coastal waters. Studies such as the one performed in Brazil's [[Abrolhos Marine National Park]] tested the direct effects of anchor damage caused by intense boating activity, and found that ''H. wrightii'' abundance was deeply impacted.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Creed |first1=Joel C |last2=Amado Filho |first2=Gilberto M |title=Disturbance and recovery of the macroflora of a seagrass (''Halodule wrightii'' Ascherson) meadow in the Abrolhos Marine National Park, Brazil: an experimental evaluation of anchor damage |journal=Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology |date=March 1999 |volume=235 |issue=2 |pages=285–306 |doi=10.1016/S0022-0981(98)00188-9 }}</ref>
